programs.title: Ancient Powers
programs.desc: The creators of the six-episode series, using advanced computer graphics, will present the history of the five most powerful civilizations of antiquity: Egypt, China, India, Rome and Greece.Ancient powers have a lot in common.In the fight for survival and domination, they went through similar stages of development.They conquered new territories, built societies and political systems, as well as formed cultures, developed trade, ideas and the art of war.Viewers will learn about the latest archaeological research on ancient powers.

programs.title: Asia: behind the scenes of production
programs.desc: Behind the scenes of a production about the fauna and flora of the largest continent on Earth.The series consists of seven episodes, and their creation took 2.5 thousand days.30 film teams were involved in the project.

programs.title: Seven Worlds, One Planet
programs.desc: Antarctica is the coldest and windiest continent.The climate here is harsh, and only the toughest can survive.From Weddell seals crushing the ice with their teeth, to colorful starfish covering the seabed hidden under the ice.Penguin chicks may lose their lives when confronted by killer whales and leopard seals.Meanwhile, starfish and huge worms line the seabed as a feeding spectacle takes place on the surface.Life comes to Antarctica because the ocean surrounding the continent is extremely rich.Thousands of penguins, seals, albatrosses and over a hundred huge whales feast on the krill schools.Unfortunately, the local waters are warming, and as the temperature increases, the future of the local fauna and flora looks more and more uncertain.

programs.title: Seven Worlds, One Planet
programs.desc: David Attenborough talks about how unique forms of life developed on different continents.
